title: Colliders & Triggers
description: Explore collider types, compound colliders, and the powerful 'Is Trigger' checkbox.

slides.title: Collider Types 📐
slides.content:
# Invisible Force Fields

Unity provides several primitive collider shapes to match your objects:

- **Box Collider** – rectangular (walls, crates).
- **Sphere Collider** – round (balls, planets).
- **Capsule Collider** – pill‑shaped (characters).
- **Mesh Collider** – matches the exact mesh geometry (expensive, use sparingly).
- **Terrain Collider** – for terrain surfaces.
- **Wheel Collider** – special for vehicles.

For 2D, there are `Collider2D` variants: BoxCollider2D, CircleCollider2D, etc.

quizData.question: Which collider type is best for a player character?
quizData.explanation: Capsule Colliders handle slopes and movement smoothly, making them ideal for characters.

slides.title: Is Trigger – The Pass‑Through Zone 🚪
slides.content:
# Detecting Without Blocking

When you check **Is Trigger** on a Collider, it no longer physically blocks objects. Instead, it fires **trigger events** when objects enter or exit its volume.

Perfect for:
- Collectibles (coins, power-ups).
- Checkpoints.
- Damage zones.
- Sensor areas (enemy sight).

Triggers are extremely lightweight because they don't involve collision resolution.

quizData.question: An object with a trigger collider will physically block other objects.
quizData.explanation: Triggers do not block; they only send events.

slides.title: Compound Colliders 🧩
slides.content:
# Combining Shapes

Sometimes a single collider can't fit your model. You can add multiple colliders to the same GameObject:
- A Box Collider for the body, a Sphere Collider for the head.
- They all act as a single physical object (since they share the same Rigidbody).
- Avoid overlapping colliders on the same object; use them for different parts.

This is much cheaper than a Mesh Collider for complex shapes.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Collider as a Child

Sometimes you want a separate GameObject just for a trigger (e.g., a large detection sphere). Make it a child object with its own collider (and maybe a small Rigidbody if needed), and use parent's scripts to react.
